title: Ultrastable de novo SuperMyo proteins enable high-performance macroscopic fibers from minimal repeats
task: Engineer computationally designed proteins with enhanced mechanostability for high-performance fibers
key_results: SuperMyo tetramers achieve tensile strength of 372 MPa and toughness of 61 MJ m⁻³, matching fibers from 64-mers with only 4 repeats; unfolding forces nearly double natural immunoglobulin domains at 1000 nm s⁻¹
comments: The paradigm shift from repeat-number to intrinsic mechanostability is elegant, though scalability of wet-spinning and long-term fiber durability remain to be demonstrated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Engineering individual domain mechanostability compensates for low repeat number in fiber performance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: tetrameric fibers match 64-mer performance

hypotheses.hypothesis: Enhanced monomer stability promotes superior β-sheet crystallization during fiber assembly
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by structural analyses

title: Chemoreceptor TRPγ coordinates locomotor activity via regulating intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis in Drosophila
task: Elucidate ligand-sensing and Ca²⁺-homeostasis mechanisms of dTRPγ chemoreceptor in behavior control
key_results: dTRPγ cryo-EM structures at 2.18 Å (apo) and 3.44 Å (camphor-bound) reveal ligand-induced pore dilation; dual allosteric Ca²⁺-sensing modules with activating (VSLD) and inhibitory (ARD-CCD) sites control locomotor kinematics (stride length and velocity)
comments: The spatial segregation of opposing Ca²⁺-sensing sites enabling bidirectional feedback is architecturally elegant, though direct in vivo Ca²⁺ dynamics imaging would strengthen the mechanistic link.

model_io.model: dTRPγ in vivo Drosophila locomotor system

hypotheses.hypothesis: dTRPγ integrates chemosensory and Ca²⁺-homeostatic signals via spatially separated allosteric modules
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: dual-feedback mechanism identified structurally and functionally validated in locomotion

hypotheses.hypothesis: Loss of Ca²⁺-regulatory function impairs adaptive locomotor behavior
hypotheses.result: Confirmed in mutant studies showing impaired locomotor activity

title: ADA2 controls autophagy-dependent mitochondrial fitness to restrain type I interferon activation

comments: Links organellar dysfunction to innate immune hyperactivation; explains immunopathogenesis of ADA2 deficiency (DADA2).
